top_choice_rationale: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles rest on a general physical-chemical design rule: a headgroup pKa near neutral in blood and cationic at endosomal pH lets nucleic acids be loaded, carried as a PEG-shielded particle and released through charge-dependent shifts in lipid packing and phase behaviour. It has been confirmed independently for years and underlies approved medicines. It is distinct from the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification, and a Cullis, Madden and Hope citation worded around the design principle is defensible, although the priority record against MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer should be checked. Base editing by Liu alone is a close second: clean attribution and genuinely new enzyme chemistry, but it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely.
recusal_note: My research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is in the same broad field as the lipid nanoparticle proposal (P002); no personal, institutional or collaborative tie to Cullis, Madden, Hope or any other credited person is apparent from my profile, so no recusal-level conflict. I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai.
